blocks.content:
A *sovereign category* is a left autonomous category endowed with a strong monoidal natural transformation $\phi_X\colon X

blocks.title: Braided categories
blocks.content:
A *braided* category is a monoidal category endowed with a *braiding*, that is, a natural isomorphism $\tau_{X,Y} \colon X \otimes Y \to Y \otimes X$ satisfying: $\tau_{X,Y\otimes Z}=(\mathrm{id}_Y \otimes \tau_{X,Z})(\tau_{X,Y} \otimes \mathrm{id}_Z)$ and $\tau_{X
\otimes Y,Z}=(\tau_{X,Z} \otimes \mathrm{id}_Y)(\mathrm{id}_X \otimes \tau_{Y,Z})$.

blocks.title: Ribbon categories
blocks.content:
A *twist* on a braided category $\mathcal{B}$ is a natural isomorphism $\theta_X \colon X \to X$ satisfying: $\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X \otimes \theta_Y)\tau_{Y,X}\tau_{X,Y}$. If $\mathcal{B}$ is braided and autonomous, a twist $\theta$ on $\mathcal{B}$ is *self-dual* if $\leftidx{^\vee}{\!(}{}\theta_X)=\theta_{\leftidx{^\vee}{\!X}{}}$ (or, equivalently, $(\theta_X{)}^\vee=\theta_{{X}^\vee}$).

A *ribbon category* is a braided autonomous category endowed with a self-dual twist. A ribbon category is naturally equipped with a sovereign structure such that the left and right traces coincide.

blocks.title: Dimension of sovereign categories
blocks.content: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a sovereign category which admits a coend. The *left* and *right dimensions of $\mathcal{C}$* are defined respectively as the left and right dimensions of its coend. These dimensions are actually independent of the choice of sovereign structure on $\mathcal{C}$. If they coincide (for instance when $\mathcal{C}$ is a ribbon category or $\mathcal{C}$ is a fusion category), they are called the *dimension of $\mathcal{C}$* and denoted $\dim \mathcal{C}$.

In this section, we review some facts on Hopf monads [@BV2].

## Monads

blocks.title: The philosophy
blocks.content:
Roughly speaking, a monad $T$ on a monoidal category $\mathcal{C}$ is a bimonad, a Hopf monad, a quasitriangular Hopf monad, or a ribbon Hopf monad if the category $T\mbox{-}\,\mathcal{C}$ of $T$-modules is respectively monoidal, autonomous, braided, or ribbon, in such a way the forgetful functor $U_T \colon T\mbox{-}\,\mathcal{C}\to \mathcal{C}$ is strict monoidal.

blocks.title: Hopf monads
blocks.content:
3.6. Hopf monads. A Hopf monad is a bimonad on an autonomous category
which has a left antipode and a right antipode.
Hopf monads generalize Hopf algebras to a non-braided (and non-linear) setting.
Furthermore they are much more general: for example, if C, D are two autonomous
categories and U : D →C is a strong monoidal functor which admits a left adjoint
F : C →D, then T = UF is a Hopf monad on C (see [BV07, corollary 3.15]).

[]{#sect-RT label="sect-RT"}

In this section, we treat in details the case of the center $\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})$ of a spherical fusion category $\mathcal{C}$. This leads to an explicit algorithm for computing Reshetikhin-Turaev-like invariants defined using $\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})$ in terms of $\mathcal{C}$.
